detailed_rationale:
Gland Pharma is India's largest sterile-injectables manufacturer, majority owned by China's Fosun Pharma, combining a US-focused (53% of FY26 group revenue) complex-generics/CDMO injectables business with Cenexi, a European CDMO arm acquired a few years ago that has been steadily turning around -- Cenexi revenue grew 25% YoY in FY26 and 22% YoY in Q4 specifically (Rs 478 cr). Group Q4 FY26 revenue grew 22% YoY to Rs 1,742.8 cr, with EBITDA up 48% YoY to Rs 510 cr (29.4% margin) -- genuine, broad-based operating improvement across both the base injectables business and the Cenexi turnaround.

Q4 PAT grew 97% YoY to Rs 370 cr, a rate well ahead of even the strong 48% EBITDA growth -- as with a couple of other names in this batch, that gap is wide enough to suggest a meaningful below-EBITDA contribution (lower finance costs, tax items, or a favourable one-off) rather than being purely a core-margin story, and I have not been able to confirm the specific driver from the sources reviewed, so the 97% figure should be treated with some caution rather than extrapolated.

The balance sheet is essentially debt-free (D/E 0.03, interest cover ~49x), but ROE (9.1%) is notably lower than ROCE (14.1%) -- consistent with a large low-yielding cash/investment balance and/or acquisition-related goodwill sitting on the balance sheet post-Cenexi, diluting equity returns without a proportionate profit contribution yet. Management's own FY27 guidance is 12-13% constant-currency revenue growth excluding potential GLP-1 (semaglutide-class) upside -- a credible, conservative base case that leaves the larger GLP-1 opportunity as genuine optionality rather than a committed forecast. At ~41x earnings, the valuation appears to be pricing meaningful GLP-1 optionality on top of the guided base growth, which is a real but genuinely uncertain (regulatory pathway, timing, competitive intensity) additional driver.
recommendation_rationale: Already a quant-Hold; the Cenexi turnaround and improving margins are real positives, but a ~41x multiple against management's own more modest 12-13% base guidance (with GLP-1 upside as unconfirmed optionality) and a PAT print that outpaced even strong EBITDA growth are enough to keep this at Hold rather than argue for anything more constructive.
summary: Gland Pharma is India's largest sterile-injectables manufacturer, benefiting from a recovering European CDMO business (Cenexi) alongside its core US-focused injectables franchise, with strong recent revenue and margin growth. The company's own growth guidance for next year is more modest than the recent quarter's headline profit growth would suggest, and part of the reported profit jump likely reflects items below the core operating line. We rate this a Hold: a well-run, debt-free business, but the valuation appears to price in upside (from potential GLP-1 drug opportunities) that is not yet guaranteed.
positive_para: Debt-free balance sheet with a genuinely improving Cenexi (European CDMO) turnaround (+25% FY26 revenue) layered onto a strong core US-focused injectables business, delivering 22% Q4 revenue growth and a 29.4% EBITDA margin. Potential GLP-1 (semaglutide-class) manufacturing opportunities represent real, large optionality beyond the base business.
negative_para: Q4 PAT growth (97%) ran well ahead of even strong EBITDA growth (48%), suggesting a meaningful below-EBITDA contribution that should not be assumed to repeat; management's own FY27 guidance of 12-13% constant-currency growth (excluding GLP-1 upside) is notably more modest than the recent quarter's headline profit growth. ROE (9.1%) trailing well behind ROCE (14.1%) suggests capital (cash, acquisition-related goodwill) that is not yet earning its keep.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~41x earnings against management's own 12-13% constant-currency base guidance, the multiple appears to price in meaningful GLP-1-related optionality on top of the base business -- a real possibility given Gland's injectables manufacturing scale, but genuinely uncertain in timing and competitive outcome. Fair-to-rich on the disclosed base case; the multiple only makes full sense if the optionality converts.
